claims.text: The onset and progression of premelting and melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by temperature-driven Cu segregation to the nanoparticle surface.
Cu is the low-melting constituent of the FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle system.
Surface Cu enrichment reduces the local cohesive energy.
Reduced local cohesive energy lowers the local melting temperature.
Cu-induced surface premelting propagates inward as heating continues.
Pre-annealing can produce a mild Cu enrichment at the surfaces of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
At elevated temperatures, Cu atoms preferentially segregate to the surfaces of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
A Cu-rich surface layer creates a premelt layer.
A Cu-rich premelt layer initiates melting at a lower temperature than in uniformly distributed FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu enrichment should be detectable before the bulk melting event.
Initially Cu-enriched nanoparticles should have a lower melting-onset temperature than compositionally uniform nanoparticles.
The uniform baseline nanoparticles show no Cu surface enrichment before melting.
The uniform baseline nanoparticles commence melting at a higher temperature than the Cu-enriched nanoparticles.
Using matched particle sizes and identical substrates isolates the influence of compositional distribution.
Heating under vacuum minimizes oxidation and other extrinsic environmental effects.
Under the specified vacuum-heating conditions, surface effects dominate the thermal response.

contradictions.description: The general hypothesis says temperature drives Cu surface segregation in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles, whereas the baseline is defined as showing no premelting Cu surface enrichment. It is unclear why the uniform baseline would not undergo the segregation proposed to govern the transition.
